g.text: NextAurora — EF Core migrations (dev vs prod split)
DEV: in-process MigrateDatabaseAsync<T>() at startup applies pending migrations.
PROD: separate pre-deploy step (multiple replicas would race if it ran in-process). The IMMUTABLE-ONCE-APPLIED rule is the load-bearing invariant.
Source: each service's Infrastructure/Data/{Service}DbContextFactory.cs · NextAurora.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs (MigrateDatabaseAsync) · each service's Program.cs
DEV ROUND-TRIP
1. Edit entity / DbContext config (e.g., add a Property, change MaxLength, add an Index)
2. dotnet ef migrations add AddPromotionCodes \
--project CatalogService
(every service is one project — same shape for
Order/Payment/Shipping: --project OrderService)
3. EF CLI uses IDesignTimeDbContextFactory to construct the DbContext OUTSIDE the running app.
CatalogDbContextFactory.CreateDbContext():
reads ConnectionStrings__catalog-db from env (Aspire injects this)
falls back to localhost dev string if env not set
returns new CatalogDbContext(options) — same context the app uses
4. EF diffs current model against ModelSnapshot.cs (the last-committed model state) and emits:
• {timestamp}_AddPromotionCodes.cs — Up()/Down() with provider-specific SQL fragments
• {timestamp}_AddPromotionCodes.Designer.cs — frozen model snapshot at this migration
• CatalogDbContextModelSnapshot.cs — updated live snapshot for the next diff
All three are added to git so the model history is reproducible.
5. dotnet run --project NextAurora.AppHost
App boots → Program.cs hits: if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment()) await app.Services.MigrateDatabaseAsync<CatalogDbContext>();
MigrateDatabaseAsync resolves the context from DI, calls Database.MigrateAsync(ct)
→ EF reads __EFMigrationsHistory table → finds AddPromotionCodes not applied → runs Up() → INSERT into __EFMigrationsHistory
Pending migrations apply in order. Done.
PROD (NOT in-process)
❌ Why NOT in-process at startup:
With multiple replicas behind a load balancer:
• replica A starts → calls Migrate → acquires the __EFMigrationsLock → applies migration
• replicas B, C start at the same time → also call Migrate → BLOCK on the lock,
THEN race: one ends up applying the same migration twice / sees the history table in flux
• Outcome: random startup failures, migration-history corruption, retry storms.
The IsDevelopment() gate exists to prevent this.
✓ Correct prod flow — SEPARATE PRE-DEPLOY STEP:
1. CI builds + tests + packages the app image
2. CI runs migrations as a one-shot job (NOT inside the app):
dotnet ef database update \
--project CatalogService \
--connection "$PROD_CATALOG_DB_CONNECTION"
This connects from CI's runner, applies pending migrations, exits.
Same EF tooling as dev — just run from a different host.
3. CI deploys the new app image to k8s / ECS / wherever.
App pods start with NO migration call (the IsDevelopment gate is false in prod).
4. Each app replica boots cleanly, schema already up-to-date.
(Tooling exists; the deployed demo migrates on startup under DemoMode —
a non-demo production deploy would automate this step in CI.)
⚠ THE IMMUTABLE-ONCE-APPLIED RULE (CLAUDE.md "Performance Rules")
Once a migration has run anywhere (including dev), it is FROZEN. Never edit it. Why: editing drifts the ModelSnapshot.cs from
the history table → next migration generation produces broken output OR (worse) deploying the edited migration to a DB that already
ran the old version either no-ops or corrupts schema.
Destructive changes (drop column / drop table / rename / NOT NULL on existing column) — DO NOT do in one migration:
Step A: Deploy code that no longer reads the column. ← deploy + wait one release cycle
Step B: Wait until all in-flight requests using the old code have completed.
Step C: Generate a new migration that drops the column. Deploy.
Doing all three in one migration is how production outages happen during deploys: old pods crash on the missing column
while new pods are still rolling out.
// What lives in each service's Migrations/ folder (committed to git)
// All services: {Service}/Infrastructure/Migrations/ (Catalog included)
20260503040949_InitialCreate.cs -- the migration class with Up() + Down() methods
20260503040949_InitialCreate.Designer.cs -- snapshot of the model AT this migration (immutable once applied)
CatalogDbContextModelSnapshot.cs -- LIVE snapshot of the current model (regenerated each migration add)
// And in the DB:
CREATE TABLE __EFMigrationsHistory ( MigrationId nvarchar(150) PK, ProductVersion nvarchar(32) );
-- Each Migrate() call: read this table, find unapplied entries, run their Up(), INSERT into this table.
Related: docs/ef-core.md §6 (Migrations) · docs/performance-and-data-correctness.md "Resolved: migration tooling wired up" · CLAUDE.md "Performance Rules" → "Migrations are immutable once applied"
